transcript.text: Good morning everyone. I've called us together today because the department has received repeated concerns around three issues: public corrections of colleagues, after-hours requests, and unclear ownership of meeting decisions. Our current department guidance doesn't specify how any of these should be handled. As VP of People, I have the authority to issue a department-wide communication charter to address these gaps — but per our established practice, I want to consult with line management, employees, team leadership, and Employee Relations before we publish anything. During that consultation, I'll need each participant to give a recorded fact report using the meeting's formal report function, and I'll wait to receive every report before making my final decision. So I'd like to hear from each of you today: what's your perspective on these three issues and what would you want to see in a communication charter?

transcript.text: I'd like to contribute a formal observation to this consultation. I have personally observed exactly 3 meetings in which a colleague was corrected in front of the group and then stopped contributing for the remainder of the meeting. I had not previously put these observations into a formal report, but I'm sharing them now as part of my recorded fact report for this consultation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I'd like to share something relevant to the after-hours requests issue. I have an agreed working boundary with my manager that urgent requests after 16:00 must be sent asynchronously — by email or message — rather than as an unscheduled call. This is because I have a recurring caregiving responsibility at that time. The agreement is recorded in my manager's notes, but it isn't reflected anywhere in the current department guidance. I think the charter should address this kind of situation so that employees aren't put in the position of having to repeatedly explain or defend individual arrangements that are already agreed with their managers.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to share something relevant to the issue of unclear ownership of meeting decisions. During last quarter's team reset, I promised the department that meeting chairs would rotate weekly and that each chair would publish the decisions afterward. However, I have not yet converted that promise into a standing process. I think this is directly relevant to the concerns about unclear ownership of meeting decisions, and I'd want the charter to formalize what I already committed to.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I'd like to contribute my recorded fact report on behalf of Employee Relations. I confirmed with Employee Relations this week that any complaints involving a manager and a direct report require a neutral ombudsperson and a review exactly 10 business days after the charter takes effect. This requirement has not yet been added to the draft charter, and I believe it must be incorporated before publication to ensure we have a proper escalation and review mechanism for the kinds of concerns being raised today.
